newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gunmen hit Russian car hours after Chechnya deal.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen hit Russian car hours after Chechnya deal.

text.p: Masked gunmen opened fire on a Russian government car in the capital of separatist-minded Chechnya on Sunday just hours after Russian and Chechen official signed a crucial oil pipeline deal, Interfax news agency said.
It quoted General Sergei Sidorenko, the Russian Interior Ministry's representative in Grozny, as saying local bodyguards returned fire and managed to break through the blockade.
"The car was hit by six bullets," Interfax quoted the general as saying. "Luckily none of those in the car was hurt."
The incident on Grozny's central Minutka square came just hours after Russian and Chechen officials signed a deal detailing how they would repair a war-damaged oil pipeline that runs across Chechnya.
Officials could not be reached from Moscow for comment.

It was not immediately clear whether there was any link between the pipeline deal and the shooting. A number of recent incidents have raised tensions after a period of relative calm and an apparent improvement in relations between Chechnya's separatist leaders and Moscow.

The pipeline deal was one example of the improved atmosphere on a political level. It is a vital conduit for Azeri oil from Caspian Sea fields to reach world markets through Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.

The general told Interfax the car was carrying local bodyguards and Vladimir Skobtsov, who works for a Russian commission set up to trace missing soldiers and prisoners of war. Russia's two-year conflict with Chechnya ended last August.

Nine Russian police died when their vehicle was blown up near Chechnya last Tuesday. At least three foreigners have been abducted in the area. Five Chechens were also seized on their way to Chechnya from the Caucasus region of North Ossetia.
Chechnya has established itself as a de facto independent entity since the war but Moscow still considers it to be one of Russia's 89 regions.
Earlier Interfax said the Russian Energy Ministry and Chechnya's YUNKO state oil company signed the detailed pipeline accord late on Saturday.

The deal would allow Russian and Chechen companies to "make the necessary contacts and sign agreements to carry out joint work on restoring and using the oil pipeline", Interfax quoted YUNKO president Khodzhakhmed Yarikhanov as saying.
The agency on Saturday quoted Chechen and Russian officials as saying work would begin in the next few days to mend the 153-km (95 mile) section of pipeline, and Moscow would pay.
Saturday's agreement was intended to flesh out a tripartite accord signed in the Azeri capital Baku on Friday.

The deal, held up for months by bickering between the sides over the details, is intended to clear the way for crude output from an $8 billion Western consortium developing off-shore Azeri Caspian Sea fields to reach world markets.
